objects.description: Opaque handle to a Xenstore connection. Only a forward declaration is provided in this header; the structure layout is private to the library. It is created by xs_open (and deprecated xs_daemon_open* / xs_domain_open) and is passed to all Xenstore operations. Must be closed with xs_close (or deprecated xs_daemon_close) and not used after destruction, including across fork unless reopened as documented.

Identifier type for Xenstore transactions. Values are returned by xs_transaction_start and passed back to most operations to scope them to a transaction. The special value XBT_NULL (0) denotes no active transaction.

Represents a Xenstore permission entry consisting of an owner/subject identifier (id) and a bitmask (perms) indicating allowed operations. The perms field uses the XS_PERM_* bit flags defined alongside the struct. Intended for use when setting or parsing access permissions in the Xenstore library/daemon. Details about the semantics of id are inferred (likely a domain or user identifier), as the header provides no additional documentation.
No custom types are defined in this header. It only emits a deprecation warning and includes xenstore_lib.h. Types from xenstore_lib.h are out of scope per instructions.

functions.name: xs_open
functions.signature: struct xs_handle *xs_open(unsigned long flags);
functions.description: Open a connection to the Xenstore daemon. Attempts a socket connection first and falls back to the xenbus/shmem interface. Use xs_open(0) for standard behavior; flags XS_OPEN_READONLY and XS_OPEN_SOCKETONLY are deprecated and ignored.
requirements: On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
Connections made with xs_open(0) are only guaranteed to work in the parent after fork.
The returned struct xs_handle* must be closed with xs_close().
Flags currently have no effect (deprecated).

functions.name: xs_close
functions.signature: void xs_close(struct xs_handle *xsh /* NULL ok */);
functions.description: Close the connection to the Xenstore daemon and release resources associated with the handle.
requirements: It is safe to pass NULL (no effect).
After calling xs_close, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: xs_daemon_open
functions.signature: struct xs_handle *xs_daemon_open(void);
functions.description: Deprecated synonym for xs_open(0). Opens a connection to the Xenstore daemon.
requirements: On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
Prefer xs_open(0) instead.
Close the returned handle with xs_close() or xs_daemon_close().

functions.name: xs_domain_open
functions.signature: struct xs_handle *xs_domain_open(void);
functions.description: Deprecated synonym for xs_open(0). Opens a connection to the Xenstore daemon (domain-aware).
requirements: On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
Prefer xs_open(0) instead.
Close the returned handle with xs_close() or xs_daemon_close().

functions.name: xs_daemon_open_readonly
functions.signature: struct xs_handle *xs_daemon_open_readonly(void);
functions.description: Deprecated API to open a Xenstore connection in read-only mode. Use xs_open(0) instead; the legacy readonly flag behavior is deprecated.
requirements: On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
Prefer xs_open(0) instead.
Close the returned handle with xs_close() or xs_daemon_close().

functions.name: xs_daemon_close
functions.signature: void xs_daemon_close(struct xs_handle *);
functions.description: Deprecated close routine for Xenstore handles. Use xs_close() instead.
requirements: Handle must be a valid xs_handle* returned by an open call.
After calling, the handle must not be used again.

functions.name: xs_daemon_destroy_postfork
functions.signature: void xs_daemon_destroy_postfork(struct xs_handle *);
functions.description: Discard an xs_handle connection in a post-fork context. Intended to throw away inherited connections that are unsafe to use in the child.
requirements: Call in a post-fork scenario where the existing connection must not be reused in the child.
Handle must be a valid xs_handle* or possibly NULL (NULL handling is not specified; treat unknown).

functions.name: xs_directory
functions.signature: char **xs_directory(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path, unsigned int *num);
functions.description: List entries in a Xenstore directory node at path within transaction t. Returns a malloced array of C strings; num receives the number of entries.
requirements: On success, returns a malloced array; caller must call free() on the returned pointer after use (each string is typically contiguous with the array; free the single block as returned).
On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
h must be a valid open handle; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().
num must be a valid pointer for output.

functions.name: xs_read
functions.signature: void *xs_read(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path, unsigned int *len);
functions.description: Read the value stored at a Xenstore node path within transaction t. Returns a malloced, NUL-terminated buffer containing the value; len is set to the length in bytes excluding the terminator.
requirements: On success, caller must free() the returned buffer.
On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().
len must be a valid pointer for output.

functions.name: xs_write
functions.signature: bool xs_write(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path, const void *data, unsigned int len);
functions.description: Write data of length len to the Xenstore node at path within transaction t.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().

functions.name: xs_write_all
functions.signature: bool xs_write_all(int fd, const void *data, unsigned int len);
functions.description: Write len bytes to the file descriptor fd, looping internally until all data are written or an error occurs.
requirements: Returns false on failure and may set errno; caller must check the boolean result.
fd must be a valid, writable file descriptor.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.

functions.name: xs_mkdir
functions.signature: bool xs_mkdir(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path);
functions.description: Create a directory node at path within transaction t. Succeeds if the directory already exists.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().

functions.name: xs_rm
functions.signature: bool xs_rm(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path);
functions.description: Remove a Xenstore node or directory (and its children) at path within transaction t. Returns false on failure or if the node does not exist.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().

functions.name: xs_restrict
functions.signature: bool xs_restrict(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned domid);
functions.description: Stub function retained for compatibility; always returns false to maintain libxenstore 3.0 behavior.
requirements: Always returns false; callers should not rely on it for access control.
h must be a (possibly unused) xs_handle*; domid is ignored.

functions.name: xs_get_permissions
functions.signature: struct xs_permissions *xs_get_permissions(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path, unsigned int *num);
functions.description: Retrieve the permissions on a Xenstore node. Returns a malloced array of xs_permissions entries. The first element represents the owner and default permissions; subsequent elements are per-domain permissions.
requirements: On success, returns a malloced array; caller must free() it after use.
num must be a valid pointer to receive the number of permissions entries.
On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().

functions.name: xs_set_permissions
functions.signature: bool xs_set_permissions(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, const char *path, struct xs_permissions *perms, unsigned int num_perms);
functions.description: Set permissions for a Xenstore node (caller must be the owner). Domain 0 bypasses permission checks. The perms array defines owner/default permissions in perms[0] and per-domain entries thereafter.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
perms must point to an array of at least num_perms xs_permissions entries; num_perms must match the array length.
If t is an active transaction, it must be started with xs_transaction_start().

functions.name: xs_watch
functions.signature: bool xs_watch(struct xs_handle *h, const char *path, const char *token);
functions.description: Register a watch on a node (and its children). When changes occur, the file descriptor from xs_fileno becomes readable; events can be obtained with xs_check_watch or xs_read_watch. The token is returned with events for correlation.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path and token must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
Call xs_unwatch with the same path and token to remove the watch.
If using XS_UNWATCH_FILTER semantics, observe the token/subpath uniqueness guidance in the header comments.

functions.name: xs_fileno
functions.signature: int xs_fileno(struct xs_handle *h);
functions.description: Return a file descriptor suitable for polling/selecting to detect pending watch events.
requirements: h must be a valid handle with an established connection.
On failure, may return a negative value and set errno (behavior not explicitly documented).
Caller must not close this fd independently of xs_close().

functions.name: xs_check_watch
functions.signature: char **xs_check_watch(struct xs_handle *h);
functions.description: Non-blocking check for pending watch events. On success returns an array of two C strings: ret[0] is the triggering path and ret[1] is the token. Returns NULL on error; when the watch fd became readable, callers should loop until this returns NULL with errno == EAGAIN.
requirements: On success, caller must free() the returned array in one call to free(ret).
On error, returns NULL and sets errno; loop until errno == EAGAIN after fd readability.
h must be valid; watch must have been registered to receive events.

functions.name: xs_read_watch
functions.signature: char **xs_read_watch(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int *num);
functions.description: Blocking retrieval of the next watch event. Returns an array containing the path and token. num receives the array length (use XS_WATCH_* to index).
requirements: On success, caller must free() the returned array with free().
On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
h must be valid; num must be a valid pointer for output.

functions.name: xs_unwatch
functions.signature: bool xs_unwatch(struct xs_handle *h, const char *path, const char *token);
functions.description: Remove a previously registered watch on path/token. Implicitly acknowledges any outstanding events for that watch.
requirements: Returns false on failure (e.g., if no such watch) and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; path and token must match those used in xs_watch().
If XS_UNWATCH_FILTER is set (global behavior), no further matching events will be delivered after xs_unwatch returns; otherwise, stale events may still be delivered.

functions.name: xs_transaction_start
functions.signature: xs_transaction_t xs_transaction_start(struct xs_handle *h);
functions.description: Begin a Xenstore transaction. Changes by others are not seen during the transaction, and changes are not visible to others until committed.
requirements: On failure, returns XBT_NULL (0) and sets errno; caller must check for this.
On success, the returned transaction must be ended with xs_transaction_end().
h must be a valid open handle.

functions.name: xs_transaction_end
functions.signature: bool xs_transaction_end(struct xs_handle *h, xs_transaction_t t, bool abort);
functions.description: End a transaction t. If abort is true, discard changes (abort); otherwise attempt to commit. On certain conflicts, it can fail with errno == EAGAIN, requiring the caller to restart the whole transaction.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; if errno == EAGAIN, the caller must restart the transaction from the beginning.
t must be a transaction previously returned by xs_transaction_start() (or XBT_NULL if not in a transaction, though this is not documented; treat as unknown).
h must be valid.
If abort is true, the transaction is discarded and not committed.

functions.name: xs_introduce_domain
functions.signature: bool xs_introduce_domain(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid, unsigned long mfn, unsigned int eventchn);
functions.description: Inform xenstored about a domain’s shared page (mfn), event channel (eventchn), and store path, enabling communication for that domain.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid.
domid, mfn, and eventchn must be valid identifiers for the target domain (detailed constraints not documented).

functions.name: xs_set_target
functions.signature: bool xs_set_target(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid, unsigned int target);
functions.description: Set the target domain that domid is allowed to manipulate in xenstored.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid.
domid and target must be valid domain IDs (exact ranges not documented).

functions.name: xs_resume_domain
functions.signature: bool xs_resume_domain(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid);
functions.description: Clear the shutdown flag for the specified domain in Xenstore (resume the domain).
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid.
domid must be a valid domain ID.

functions.name: xs_release_domain
functions.signature: bool xs_release_domain(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid);
functions.description: Ask xenstored to release the shared memory page for the specified domain.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid.
domid must be a valid domain ID.

functions.name: xs_get_domain_path
functions.signature: char *xs_get_domain_path(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid);
functions.description: Query the home Xenstore path for the specified domain. Returns a malloced string containing the path.
requirements: On success, caller must free() the returned string.
On failure, returns NULL and sets errno; caller must check for NULL.
h must be valid; domid must be a valid domain ID.

functions.name: xs_path_is_subpath
functions.signature: bool xs_path_is_subpath(const char *parent, const char *child);
functions.description: Return true if child is equal to parent or is a node under parent, based on string comparison; false otherwise. Relative and absolute paths are never parent/child by this definition. Cannot fail.
requirements: parent and child must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
Function cannot fail; does not set errno.

functions.name: xs_is_domain_introduced
functions.signature: bool xs_is_domain_introduced(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid);
functions.description: Check whether the specified domain has been introduced to xenstored.
requirements: Returns true if introduced; false otherwise (on failure or not introduced); on failure, errno may be set (not explicitly documented).
h must be valid; domid must be a valid domain ID.

functions.name: xs_get_features_supported
functions.signature: bool xs_get_features_supported(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int *features);
functions.description: Query the feature bitmap supported by xenstored. On success, writes a bitmap of XENSTORE_SERVER_FEATURE_* values to features.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; features must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the bitmap.

functions.name: xs_get_features_domain
functions.signature: bool xs_get_features_domain(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid, unsigned int *features);
functions.description: Get the feature bitmap available to a given domain.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; domid must be valid; features must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the bitmap.

functions.name: xs_set_features_domain
functions.signature: bool xs_set_features_domain(struct xs_handle *h, unsigned int domid, unsigned int features);
functions.description: Set the feature bitmap available for a given domain.
requirements: Returns false on failure and sets errno; caller must check the boolean result.
h must be valid; domid must be valid.
features is a bitmap; valid bit meanings are XENSTORE_SERVER_FEATURE_* (exact constraints not documented).

functions.name: xs_control_command
functions.signature: char *xs_control_command(struct xs_handle *h, const char *cmd, void *data, unsigned int len);

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated string representing a path-like key, typically absolute (starting with '/') for Xenstore nodes. May contain slashes to denote hierarchy; treated as a generic filesystem-style path.
An opaque byte buffer of arbitrary contents and length; not required to be valid text or follow any encoding. Used for payloads or value data.
A short NUL-terminated string used as an opaque token/identifier for correlating events or registrations. No specific format required.
A NUL-terminated ASCII/UTF-8 text command keyword sent to a control/debug interface. Content is free-form but expected to be textual command names or arguments.

A NUL-terminated textual specification describing permission entries for Xenstore. Format is implementation-defined (e.g., owner and per-domain entries with read/write flags), potentially multiple entries encoded in a single string.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Xenstore-like filesystem path strings and related tokens/data.
# Targets FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses in stubs for:
# - paths (mostly absolute, limited length), tokens (arbitrary strings), and data payload (arbitrary bytes).
# We pack multiple interesting strings into one bytes buffer separated by NUL so that
# consecutive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls consume them in order. We also include some
# extra entries to allow the fuzzer to pull additional strings when needed.
#
# Layout (all NUL-terminated C strings, concatenated):
#   [path1]\0[path2]\0[data]\0[token1]\0[token2]\0[parent]\0[child]\0... possibly more
# Each component is crafted to be valid and exercise different behaviors.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ABS_PREFIXES = [
    "/",                     # root
    "/local",                # typical xenstore subtree
    "/tool",                 # toolstack subtree
    "/vm",                   # VMs
    "/devices",              # devices
    "/xapi",                 # other mgmt stacks
]

REL_PREFIXES = [
    "domU", "dom0", "tmp", "var", "etc"
]

COMP_ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
COMP_SAFE = COMP_ALNUM + "-_:.@"

def _rand_comp(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(COMP_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def _path_abs(r: random.Random, max_segs=6) -> str:
    # Build an absolute path with 1..max_segs components.
    base = r.choice(ABS_PREFIXES)
    segs = r.randint(0, max_segs)
    parts = [base]
    for _ in range(segs):
        parts.append(_rand_comp(r))
    p = '/'.join(s.strip('/') for s in parts if s != '/')
    if not p.startswith('/'):
        p = '/' + p
    return p

def _path_rel(r: random.Random, max_segs=4) -> str:
    base = r.choice(REL_PREFIXES)
    segs = r.randint(0, max_segs)
    parts = [base] + [_rand_comp(r) for _ in range(segs)]
    return '/'.join(parts)

def _with_trailing_slash(r: random.Random, p: str) -> str:
    return p if r.random() < 0.5 else (p.rstrip('/') + '/')

def _maybe_duplicate_sep(r: random.Random, p: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally insert // between components to test normalization behavior safely
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        return p.replace('/', '//', 1)
    return p

def _bounded(s: str, limit: int) -> str:
    if len(s) <= limit:
        return s
    # keep head and tail with an ellipsis-like marker to remain valid
    head = s[: max(1, limit - 10)]
    return head

def _make_token(r: random.Random, limit=128) -> str:
    # Arbitrary token string; may include spaces and punctuation but avoid NUL
    alphabet = COMP_SAFE + " +#,$%^&*()[]{}""'" + "~"
    n = r.randint(0, min(64, limit))
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _make_data(r: random.Random, limit=512) -> str:
    # Data payload as a UTF-8 friendly string; may include newlines and binary-ish escapes
    # Avoid NUL to keep single C-string; fuzzer passes length separately.
    alphabet = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if c != '\\0') + "\n\t\r"
    n = r.randint(0, limit)
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _interesting_pairs(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # For xs_path_is_subpath tests: generate pairs covering equal, parent, sibling, relative, and absolute/relative mixes.
    pairs = []
    parent = _path_abs(r)
    child_under = parent.rstrip('/') + '/' + _rand_comp(r)
    pairs.extend([parent, child_under])

    # Equal paths
    eq = _path_abs(r)
    pairs.extend([eq, eq])

    # Sibling vs parent
    p2 = _path_abs(r)
    sib1 = p2.rstrip('/') + '/' + _rand_comp(r)
    sib2 = p2.rstrip('/') + '/' + _rand_comp(r)
    pairs.extend([sib1, sib2])

    # Relative paths (never parent/child by definition in header)
    relp = _path_rel(r)
    relc = relp + '/' + _rand_comp(r)
    pairs.extend([relp, relc])

    # Absolute vs relative
    pairs.extend([_path_abs(r), _path_rel(r)])

    # Trailing slash variants
    base = _path_abs(r)
    pairs.extend([_with_trailing_slash(r, base), base])

    # Mixed double slashes
    base2 = _maybe_duplicate_sep(r, _path_abs(r))
    pairs.extend([base2, base2.rstrip('/') + '/' + _rand_comp(r)])

    return pairs

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    out: List[bytes] = []

    # Primary paths used by mkdir/write/read/rm/get_permissions/set_permissions/watch/unwatch
    # Create a few absolute paths of varying depth
    paths = []
    for _ in range(5):
        p = _path_abs(r)
        p = _maybe_duplicate_sep(r, p)
        p = _with_trailing_slash(r, p)
        p = _bounded(p, 256)
        if not p.startswith('/'):
            p = '/' + p
        paths.append(p)

    # Include some fixed-interesting paths commonly present in Xenstore
    fixed = [
        "/", "/local/domain/0", "/tool", "/vm", "/devices", "/local/domain/0/name",
    ]
    for p in fixed:
        paths.append(_bounded(p, 256))

    # Data payload for xs_write
    data = _make_data(r, 512)

    # Tokens for xs_watch/xs_unwatch
    tokens = [_make_token(r, 128) for _ in range(3)]

    # Pairs for xs_path_is_subpath repeated calls
    pairs = _interesting_pairs(r)

    # Assemble order roughly matching consumption: many stubs start with path
    for p in paths:
        out.append(p.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Provide a data buffer next (used by xs_write)
    out.append(data.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Tokens
    for t in tokens:
        out.append(t.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Add multiple parent/child pairs
    for s in pairs:
        out.append(s.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # Ensure total size bound
    blob = b"".join(out)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL - 1] + b"\x00"

    return blob

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets fuzzer stubs that use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to build:
# - Xenstore absolute paths (must start with '/') with max len ~256
# - Command strings (non-empty, <=128)
# - Optional binary payloads (<=512)
# - Arbitrary data values for xs_write (<=512)
# The harness will request strings/filenames repeatedly; we provide a single
# buffer containing multiple, clearly delimited sections so the fuzzer can
# split or reuse segments to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR and optional payloads.
# The data are VALID inputs: well-formed absolute paths and sensible command
# tokens, plus arbitrary but coherent binary payloads.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMAND_CORPUS = [
    # Common xenstored control/debug commands across implementations
    b"get-perms", b"set-perms", b"get-domain-path", b"introduce",
    b"resume", b"release", b"is-introduced", b"get-features",
    b"set-features", b"debug", b"help", b"version",
    # Edge-ish tokens and variants
    b"\x00",  # though FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely stops at NUL, include for variety
    b"x", b"cmd", b"noop", b"echo", b"stats"
]

# Build interesting absolute paths exercising different shapes.
# Xenstore uses Unix-like key paths.
PATH_PREFIXES = [b"/", b"/local", b"/tool", b"/vm", b"/xen", b"/libxl",
                 b"/device", b"/device/vif", b"/device/vbd", b"/attr",
                 b"/data", b"/error", b"/transactions"]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:."  # safe for paths/cmds
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(l)).encode('ascii')

def _rand_blob(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix texty and binary bytes
    blob = bytearray()
    for _ in range(l):
        if rng.random() < 0.75:
            blob.append(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7e))  # printable ASCII
        else:
            blob.append(rng.randint(0x00, 0xff))
    return bytes(blob)

def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Ensure absolute path starting with '/'; length cap 256 in stub
    base = rng.choice(PATH_PREFIXES)
    parts = []
    # Variable depth 0..6
    depth = rng.randint(0, 6)
    for _ in range(depth):
        # Sometimes include numbers/hex-like, domainish segments
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            parts.append(b"dom-" + str(rng.randint(0, 4095)).encode())
        elif choice < 0.4:
            parts.append(b"vm-" + _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 8))
        elif choice < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 10))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            parts.append(b"uuid-" + _rand_ascii(rng, 8, 8))
        else:
            parts.append(b"k" + str(rng.getrandbits(16)).encode())
    path = base
    for p in parts:
        if not path.endswith(b"/"):
            path += b"/"
        path += p
    # Occasionally end with slash or a key-like leaf
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and not path.endswith(b"/"):
        # Add a leaf name
        leaf = rng.choice([b"name", b"state", b"backend", b"frontend",
                           b"read", b"write", b"features", b"control",
                           b"ring", b"event-channel"]) + (
            b"-" + _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6) if rng.random() < 0.3 else b""
        )
        if not path.endswith(b"/"):
            path += b"/"
        path += leaf
    elif rng.random() < 0.2:
        path += b"/"
    # Cap to 256
    return path[:256]

def _build_command(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        cmd = rng.choice(COMMAND_CORPUS)
        if cmd == b"\x00":
            # Avoid empty result after C-string parsing; replace with 'x'
            return b"x"
        return cmd[:128]
    # Random token-like command
    return _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32)[:128]

def _section(tag: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Tag (4 bytes) + length (u16 LE) + payload; keeps total under MAX_TOTAL
    l = len(payload)
    if l > 0xFFFF:
        payload = payload[:0xFFFF]
        l = len(payload)
    return tag + struct.pack('<H', l) + payload

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # Produce multiple candidate paths, commands, and payloads for the harness
    num_paths = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(num_paths):
        sections.append(_section(b"PATH", _build_path(rng)))

    num_cmds = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(num_cmds):
        sections.append(_section(b"CMD\x00", _build_command(rng)))

    # Data buffers for xs_write values (<=512)
    num_data = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(num_data):
        # Mix sizes: small, medium, edge 0 and 512
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.1:
            payload = b""  # zero-length valid data
        elif roll < 0.2:
            payload = _rand_blob(rng, 512, 512)  # exact cap
        elif roll < 0.6:
            payload = _rand_blob(rng, 1, 64)
        else:
            payload = _rand_blob(rng, 65, 512)
        sections.append(_section(b"DATA", payload))

    # Optional binary payloads for control/debug commands
    num_pl = rng.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(num_pl):
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.3:
            payload = b""  # triggers NULL/0 path in harness sometimes
        else:
            payload = _rand_blob(rng, 1, 512)
        sections.append(_section(b"PLD\x00", payload))

    # Add a compact index header for convenience: counts of each kind
    header = struct.pack(
        '<4sHHHH', b'XSIN', num_paths, num_cmds, num_data, num_pl
    )

    out = header + b''.join(sections)
    return out[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Xenstore watch/unwatch fuzzers expecting strings:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR supplies both the path and the token in these stubs.
# - The stub ensures:
#   * path is absolute: it will prepend '/' if missing; we should often provide valid absolute paths already
#   * max lengths: path <= 256, token <= 128 after stub-side truncation
# - Interesting valid inputs include:
#   * various absolute paths with differing depths and characters
#   * well-known xenstore-like prefixes (e.g., /local/domain/<id>/, /tool, /vm)
#   * edge cases: root '/', empty token, repeated slashes, trailing slashes
#   * matching pairs of path+token likely to hit success paths across calls
# Since our generator only returns one buffer consumed by successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls,
# we will encode multiple candidate strings separated by NUL bytes, letting the fuzzer framework
# consume them sequentially. Remaining reads will yield empty strings (still valid; stub will prefix '/').

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:.@+"

# Some realistic xenstore path bases
BASES = [
    "/",  # root
    "/local/domain/",
    "/local/domain/0/",
    "/vm/",
    "/tool/",
    "/device/",
    "/libxl/",
    "/xapi/",
]

LEAFS = [
    "name", "state", "backend", "frontend", "console", "device-model",
    "hotplug", "control", "data", "features", "params", "status",
]

TOKENS_COMMON = [
    "",  # empty token is allowed
    "t", "watch", "unwatch", "evt", "dom0", "domU",
    "alpha123", "TOKEN-001", "pathmatch", "*",
]


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def make_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a plausible absolute xenstore path, bounded to ~200 chars
    base = rng.choice(BASES)
    path = base
    # If base is just '/', we may add segments; if base already ends with '/', keep appending
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    # Sometimes choose a domain id segment if base expects it
    if base.endswith("/local/domain/"):
        path += str(rng.randint(0, 1024)) + "/"
    # Add additional segments
    for _ in range(depth):
        seg_choice = rng.randint(0, 3)
        if seg_choice == 0:
            seg = rng.choice(LEAFS)
        elif seg_choice == 1:
            seg = rand_ident(rng, 1, 12)
        else:
            # numeric segment like domain id or index
            seg = str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))
        # Occasionally add repeated slashes or trailing slash later
        path += seg + "/"
    # Optionally end at a leaf without trailing slash
    if path != "/" and rng.random() < 0.6:
        # remove last slash
        if path.endswith("/"):
            path = path[:-1]
    # Introduce occasional repeated slashes (still valid for many string compares in callers)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = path.replace("//", "/")  # normalize first
        insert_pos = rng.randint(1, max(1, len(path)-1))
        path = path[:insert_pos] + "/" + path[insert_pos:]
    # Ensure absolute and length bound (<256 as per stub cap)
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        path = "/" + path
    if len(path) > 250:
        path = path[:250]
    return path


def make_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Make short NUL-terminated identifier strings; the fuzzer stub caps at 128.
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        return rng.choice(TOKENS_COMMON)
    elif choice < 0.4:
        return rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        return rand_ident(rng, 9, 24)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        # include path-like token to test correlation handling
        return "tok-" + rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)
    else:
        # numeric token
        return str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))


def build_sequence(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> List[bytes]:
    seq: List[bytes] = []
    # Create interleaved pairs: path, token, possibly more pairs to exercise multiple calls
    for _ in range(count):
        p = make_path(rng)
        t = make_token(rng)
        seq.append(p.encode('utf-8'))
        seq.append(t.encode('utf-8'))
    # Add a couple of matching repeats to allow xs_unwatch to potentially match an earlier watch
    if seq:
        # Duplicate a prior pair
        idx = rng.randrange(0, len(seq)//2) * 2
        seq.append(seq[idx])
        seq.append(seq[idx+1])
    return seq


def pack_cstrings(items: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NULs, and ensure final NUL termination so subsequent reads can still get empty strings
    out = b"\x00".join(items) + b"\x00"
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure termination
        if not out.endswith(b"\x00"):
            out = out[:-1] + b"\x00"
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide how many path/token pairs to include; each pair contributes two C-strings
    pair_count = rng.randint(2, 6)
    seq = build_sequence(rng, pair_count)
    # Include some extras to cover edge cases: root path and empty token, and an extremely short token
    seq.extend([
        b"/", b"",  # root with empty token
        b"/local/domain/0", b"dom0",
        b"/vm/" + rand_ident(rng,1,8).encode('utf-8'), b"t",
    ])
    return pack_cstrings(seq)

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator focuses on producing valid, interesting command strings (and optional payloads)
# for xs_control_command/xs_debug_command fuzzers. The fuzzer obtains:
# - cmd via FUZZ_PARAM_STR() (truncated to 128 and forced non-empty)
# - possibly a payload via FUZZ_PARAM_STR() (truncated to 512) gated by a random unsigned int
# We therefore produce a single bytes buffer encoded as:
# [u32 flags][u32 cmd_len][cmd bytes][u32 payload_len][payload bytes]
# Where:
# - flags bit0 decides whether a payload is provided (matches fuzzer's branch)
# - cmd_len in [1,128]
# - payload_len in [0,512] (0 allowed but only used if flags bit0==1; if bit0==0 we set payload_len=0 and omit payload bytes)
# The strings are UTF-8 textual commands, with a corpus including common/interesting command names and arguments
# that are likely valid for xenstored control/debug channels (typical in-tree commands vary by build, but we
# include broadly plausible verbs and admin/debug knobs).
# The output is a single contiguous buffer <= 4096 bytes.

_CMD_KEYWORDS = [
    # generic admin/debug commands often found across daemon control interfaces
    "help", "version", "ping", "stats", "status", "dump", "reload", "reconfigure",
    "log", "loglevel", "set-log-level", "trace", "gc", "mempool-stats",
    # xenstored/xenstore related plausible commands
    "get-perms", "set-perms", "get-domain-path", "watch", "unwatch", "list", "ls",
    "read", "write", "mkdir", "rm", "get-features", "set-features", "introduce",
    "release-domain", "resume-domain", "is-domain-introduced", "set-target",
    # debug/experimental knobs
    "debug", "debug-keys", "enable-feature", "disable-feature", "feature-bitmap",
]

# Some argument fragments for command construction
_ARG_FRAGMENTS = [
    "domid=0", "domid=1", "domid=42", "target=0", "target=7",
    "path=/", "path=/local/domain/0", "path=/tool", "path=/vm/0000-0000",
    "token=t0", "token=alpha", "token=watch-✶",
    "perms=ro", "perms=rw", "id=0", "id=42",
    "key=k1", "key=long-key", "value=on", "value=off", "value=hello",
    "mfn=0", "eventchn=10",
]

# Some payload templates with binary-friendly content (still valid as bytes)
_PAYLOAD_TEMPLATES: List[bytes] = [
    b"",  # empty allowed
    b"ok\n",
    b"true",
    b"false",
    b"rw",
    b"ro",
    b"value=on\n",
    b"value=off\n",
    b"{\"op\":\"set\",\"key\":\"k1\",\"value\":\"v\"}",
    b"path=/local/domain/0\n",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:./=, +"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _build_cmd(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a command with keyword and optional arguments
    kw = rng.choice(_CMD_KEYWORDS)
    # Decide argument style
    style = rng.randrange(4)
    parts = [kw]
    if style == 0:
        # No args
        pass
    elif style == 1:
        # One or two known fragments
        parts += rng.sample(_ARG_FRAGMENTS, k=rng.randint(1, 2))
    elif style == 2:
        # Key/value CLI-ish: kw key value
        k = rng.choice(["key", "path", "token", "domid", "target", "perms"])  # simple keys
        v = rng.choice([
            "/", "/local/domain/0", "/tool", "/vm/0000-0000", "0", "1", "42", "rw", "ro", "alpha"
        ])
        parts += [k, v]
    else:
        # Mixed: known fragments + random tail
        parts += rng.sample(_ARG_FRAGMENTS, k=rng.randint(1, 3))
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12))
    cmd = ' '.join(parts)
    # Enforce non-empty and length <=128; fuzzer will truncate further if longer
    if not cmd:
        cmd = "x"
    if len(cmd) > 128:
        cmd = cmd[:128]
    return cmd

def _build_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 512) -> bytes:
    # Choose between template, repeated pattern, utf-8 text, or small binary span
    choice = rng.randrange(4)
    if choice == 0:
        data = rng.choice(_PAYLOAD_TEMPLATES)
    elif choice == 1:
        # UTF-8 text payload resembling a config or kv pairs
        parts = []
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        for _ in range(n):
            k = rng.choice(["key", "value", "path", "domid", "token", "perms"])  # simple keys
            v = rng.choice([
                "on", "off", "0", "1", "42", "/", "/local/domain/0", "alpha", "rw", "ro"
            ])
            parts.append(f"{k}={v}")
        data = ('\n'.join(parts) + '\n').encode('utf-8')
    elif choice == 2:
        # Repeated deterministic pattern
        pat = rng.choice([b"A", b"AB", b"0123456789", b"rw", b"ro"]) \
              * rng.randint(1, 64)
        data = pat
    else:
        # Small binary with some structured numbers
        nums = [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8))]
        data = b"BIN\x00" + b"".join(struct.pack("<I", n) for n in nums)
    if len(data) > max_len:
        data = data[:max_len]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether to include payload (bit0 like the fuzzer does)
    include_payload = rng.choice([True, False])
    flags = 1 if include_payload else 0

    cmd = _build_cmd(rng)
    cmd_bytes = cmd.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if not cmd_bytes:
        cmd_bytes = b"x"
    if len(cmd_bytes) > 128:
        cmd_bytes = cmd_bytes[:128]

    if include_payload:
        payload = _build_payload(rng, 512)
    else:
        payload = b""

    # Construct buffer: [flags][cmd_len][cmd][payload_len][payload]
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += struct.pack('<I', flags)
    buf += struct.pack('<I', len(cmd_bytes))
    buf += cmd_bytes
    buf += struct.pack('<I', len(payload))
    buf += payload

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return bytes(buf)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Xenstore permissions specification strings for xs_strings_to_perms.
# The exact grammar is implementation-defined in different libxenstore versions, but
# historically supported forms include combinations like:
#   - owner:<domid> [r][w]
#   - <domid>:[r][w]
#   - dom<domid>:[r][w]
#   - <domid> r,w   or  <domid> = rw
#   - comma/space/semicolon separated lists
#   - tokens like "READ", "WRITE", "+r", "-w"
#   - hex/octal ids, signed/unsigned variants
# To maximize valid parses across variants, we synthesize strings using a mixture
# of common patterns and separators while keeping the whole buffer under 4096 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Common separators that many parsers accept between entries
ENTRY_SEPS = [",", ";", " ", "\n", "\t", "  ", " , ", " ; "]

# Permission encodings seen across implementations
PERM_PATTERNS = [
    "rw",           # both
    "r",            # read
    "w",            # write
    "",             # none / owner-only depending on context
    "READ",         # verbose tokens
    "WRITE",
    "READ|WRITE",
    "r|w",
    "r,w",
    "+r+w",
    "+r",
    "+w",
    "-r",
    "-w",
]

# Entry patterns. We create several forms to hit different branches in parsers.
# Placeholders: {id} and {perms}
ENTRY_PATTERNS = [
    "{id}:{perms}",            # simple colon separation
    "owner:{id} {perms}",      # explicit owner keyword
    "dom{idd}:{perms}",        # dom-prefixed id
    "{id}={perms}",            # equals style
    "{id} {perms}",            # space separated
    "{id}({perms})",           # parentheses
    "{id}[{perms}]",           # brackets
    "id={id};perms={perms}",   # key=value pairs
]

# Some whitespace variants to exercise tokenization
WS = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "  "]


def _rand_domid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of decimal, hex, and signed-looking values; many parsers accept unsigned
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF))
    if choice == 1:
        return hex(rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF))  # e.g., 0x1af
    if choice == 2:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 2**31 - 1))
    if choice == 3:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 100))  # small common domids
    return str(rng.randint(0, 4096))


def _rand_perms(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(PERM_PATTERNS)
    # Occasionally mix cases or add surrounding whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = base.upper()
    elif rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = base.lower()
    # Sometimes expand symbolic rw into verbose format for diversity
    if base == "rw" and rng.random() < 0.4:
        base = "READ,WRITE"
    # Optionally insert spaces around separators
    base = base.replace(",", rng.choice([",", ", ", " , "]))
    base = base.replace("|", rng.choice(["|", " | "]))
    # Optionally empty perms (some entries may only set owner)
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        base = ""
    return base


def _make_entry(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pid = _rand_domid(rng)
    perms = _rand_perms(rng)
    pat = rng.choice(ENTRY_PATTERNS)
    # For the dom{idd} pattern, ensure a pure decimal id for readability
    idd = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    entry = pat.format(id=pid, idd=pid, perms=perms)
    # Random surrounding whitespace
    pre = rng.choice(WS)
    post = rng.choice(WS)
    return f"{pre}{entry}{post}"


def _compose_spec(rng: random.Random, target_entries: int) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Frequently include an explicit owner first to satisfy parsers that expect it.
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        owner_id = _rand_domid(rng)
        owner_perm = rng.choice(["rw", "r", "w", "READ,WRITE", "READ", "WRITE"]) if rng.random() < 0.9 else ""
        parts.append(f"owner:{owner_id} {owner_perm}".strip())
    # Add additional entries
    for _ in range(max(0, target_entries - len(parts))):
        parts.append(_make_entry(rng))
    # Join with varied separators
    spec = ""
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        if i:
            spec += rng.choice(ENTRY_SEPS)
        spec += p
    # Occasionally wrap whole spec in extraneous whitespace
    spec = rng.choice(WS) + spec + rng.choice(WS)
    # Cap length to MAX_BYTES-1 for NUL terminator safety in consumers
    return spec[: MAX_BYTES - 1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a bounded number of permission entries (the fuzzer caps at <16)
    num = rng.randint(0, 15)
    spec = _compose_spec(rng, num if num > 0 else rng.randint(1, 8))

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes with NUL terminator probability; some parsers only
    # read up to the first NUL through c_str() anyway, but explicit termination
    # can help ensure exact boundaries in some harnesses.
    data = spec.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    if len(data) >= MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[: MAX_BYTES - 1]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        data += b"\x00"
    return data
